title: The Power Goes Out for 3 Days. Pip Has 1 Hour.
description:
A storm is coming and the power could be out for three days. Pip has one hour to get ready, and he gets almost everything wrong first.

What you'll learn:
- Store about 4 liters (1 gallon) of water per person per day
- A closed fridge keeps food cold for about 4 hours, a full freezer about 48 hours
- Use flashlights, not candles
- Never run a generator indoors or in a garage
sources: USDA - Food Safety During Power Outage

scenes.narration: Pip's phone buzzes. Storm warning. Power outages expected for up to three days. Pip has one hour.
scenes.image_prompt: Pip sitting on a sofa staring at a buzzing phone, eyes wide in panic

scenes.narration: His first thought: snacks. Wrong. The first thing you need is water.
scenes.image_prompt: Pip proudly holding a giant bag of chips, a big red X drawn over it

scenes.narration: The rule is about one gallon, roughly four liters, per person, per day. For three days, Pip needs twelve liters.
scenes.image_prompt: Pip standing next to three large water jugs lined up

scenes.narration: He fills every bottle he owns, then fills the bathtub. That water isn't for drinking. It's for flushing the toilet.
scenes.image_prompt: Pip filling a bathtub with water, a toilet nearby

scenes.narration: Forty five minutes left. Food. Pip opens the fridge and panics.
scenes.image_prompt: Pip in front of an open fridge, light spilling out, hands on his head

scenes.narration: Here's the trick. A closed fridge keeps food cold for about four hours. A full freezer, about two days. So keep the doors shut.
scenes.image_prompt: Pip taping the fridge door closed with a determined face
